one_line: A human-approved, wallet-backed agent flow for purchasing licensed publisher content.
what_it_does: Galleon lets an agent inspect a source offer, obtain human approval, purchase with constrained test credits, and unlock the cited article.
leverage_rationale: Structured offers, rights, payment policy, idempotency, entitlement scope, and canonical citation make the agent-mediated purchase materially safer and more precise than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies inspect_source, human approval, purchase_offer, and unlock_source as a shared flow.
Frame sheet shows transition from the dark 'How Codex pays for knowledge' surface to a content/workspace state, though calls are not legible.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent end-to-end prototype and the frames show a polished product surface plus a resulting content/workspace state, but no readable purchase confirmation is visible.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion frame sheets are present.
About text describes authenticated wallet, spending limits, purchase recording, entitlement, and citation return.
Frame evidence does not clearly show a completed transaction.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete creator-economy problem: agents need authoritative content while publishers need compensation, with human control over price and rights.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about text identify publishers, agents, licensed access, canonical citations, and human approval.
Test-credit prototype is explicitly disclosed.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-readable pricing, explicit rights, constrained wallet authority, and source-scoped entitlements is a memorable and ambitious use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: The packet presents a novel publisher-to-agent paid-source protocol.
The flow separates publisher page, local wallet authority, approval, and entitlement redemption.
usability_note: The approval flow is understandable, but the visual packet does not establish the full operational path.
red_flags: Prototype uses test credits; completed purchase is not clearly visible in the frame sheets.
standouts: Strong human-controlled payment and rights model for agent content access.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-leverage protocol concept with credible value and substantial implementation detail.

one_line: A mission-control dashboard where agents propose and humans approve verified task transitions.
what_it_does: Mission Center exposes task state, dependencies, evidence, proposals, verification, and audit history to browser agents while keeping lifecycle changes human-gated.
leverage_rationale: Semantic task/evidence access and proposal-only mutations are substantially more reliable than pixel automation for reviewable workflow transitions, though the mission domain remains UI-replicable in principle.
leverage_evidence: About text describes eight tools sharing live state, evidence, proposal queue, approval UI, and audit trail.
Frame sheet visibly shows agent-proposal, human-decision, verification, and tool-related panels.
execution_rationale: The central proposal-to-revalidate-to-approve workflow is coherent and visibly represented, with strong stated safeguards and testing; the final Done transition is described more clearly than shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show a consistent mission-control UI with proposal, pending human decision, and verification states.
About text states deterministic Node tests, revision checks, evidence gates, and deployment workflow.
impact_rationale: Teams managing consequential work benefit from auditable agent assistance without surrendering authority over task truth.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies task review, evidence freshness, dependency inspection, safe next moves, and human approval as the target use case.
Audit trail and revalidation directly address trust in agent workflows.
creativity_rationale: The proposal-only agent and explicit evidence/revision gate are a thoughtful interaction model for human-in-command operations.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes while human decides is built into the product semantics, not merely presented as chat.
Separate agent calls, proposals, and human decisions are auditable.
usability_note: The staged mission console and approval language are clear, though dense operational panels may require learning.
red_flags: No public repository; exact tool payloads are not legible in the contact sheet.
standouts: Strong safety boundary between agent proposal and human lifecycle authority.
advance_reason: Well-grounded human-in-command workflow with strong WebMCP semantics and visible product-state progression.

one_line: A shared, approval-driven studio for agents and humans to create launch videos.
what_it_does: PrismLaunch turns a product brief into concepts, scripts, storyboards, style frames, animatics, and an editable timeline while recording approvals and revisions.
leverage_rationale: Structured operations over a staged video project and shared timeline avoid fragile screenshot editing and make iterative agent revisions reviewable and repeatable.
leverage_evidence: About text names stages, shared timeline, tool calls, captured frames, revisions, and approvals.
Frames visibly show prompt, brief, concept, script, approval cards, preview, assets, and timeline states.
execution_rationale: The motion evidence shows a coherent progression from prompt through multiple creative artifacts into an editor with preview, scenes, assets, and timeline; final export quality is not established.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows discrete Brief, Concept, and Script states with Approve/Send back controls.
Later frames show an actual video-editor workspace, generated scenes, preview, and timeline.
About text describes modular project files and saved activity.
impact_rationale: Small product teams and builders have a real need to produce launch videos without mastering motion-graphics software, and the staged workflow directly addresses that bottleneck.
impact_evidence: Pitch and inspiration identify product builders who need promotional video support.
The demonstrated workflow covers the practical path from message to editable film.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent creative-directing model, with approval at each artifact stage and a persistent editable film, is a fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Agent-generated brief, concept, script, storyboard, style frames, and animatic are separately reviewable.
Human directs the same timeline rather than receiving a black-box video.
usability_note: Approval checkpoints and familiar timeline editing make the complex workflow legible.
red_flags: Contact sheets do not show explicit named tool-call logs or final export.
standouts: Most complete visible creative-production pipeline in the packet.
advance_reason: Strong end-to-end product evidence, meaningful agent leverage, and an ambitious creative workflow.

one_line: A collaborative workspace where an agent and human build and export narrated product demos.
what_it_does: DemoMotion accepts a web app and goal, plans a scenario, records via Playwright, creates narration, renders MP4, and exposes shared editing and export tools.
leverage_rationale: Semantic demo creation and narration/editing operations give the agent reliable access to a multi-step production pipeline and shared state instead of fragile UI manipulation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies get_demo_state, create_demo, update_demo_narration, generate_demo, and human-gated export_demo.
Frames show the DemoMotion x WebMCP workspace alongside an interaction surface, though exact calls are unreadable.
execution_rationale: The described pipeline and shared workspace are substantial, but the contact sheet mainly shows the integration panel and does not clearly demonstrate a completed rendered demo/export.
execution_evidence: Three motion frame sheets show a persistent WebMCP workspace and changing interaction states.
About text claims existing FastAPI pipeline reuse and same-source-of-truth UI/tool handlers.
No clear final MP4 result is visible.
impact_rationale: Product teams have a concrete need for faster, repeatable narrated demos, and the workflow targets the painful gap between web-app knowledge and video production.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies human-agent production of narrated product demos.
About text describes browser recording, narration, voice, rendering, and export.
creativity_rationale: The shared editable demo workspace and human-gated export are a compelling application of WebMCP to product communication.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human mutate the same demo fields with visible activity log.
WebMCP is presented as an adapter to real pipeline services rather than a fake chat layer.
usability_note: The intended workflow is clear, but the dense integration panel is difficult to assess from the frames.
red_flags: Contact sheet does not clearly show generated video or export completion.
standouts: Connects structured agent operations to a real browser-recording and rendering pipeline.
advance_reason: High-value workflow and strong claimed implementation, with moderate deduction for thin visible end-state evidence.

one_line: An agent-native gaming platform that assembles multiplayer sessions from group constraints.
what_it_does: Captain Claw lets an agent inspect friends, presence, libraries, catalog metadata, play history, and session fit, then create parties and send invitations for human-approved launch.
leverage_rationale: The agent must join structured social, ownership, availability, catalog, and session data to coordinate a group; general UI driving would be markedly less reliable and precise.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 13 tools spanning presence, libraries, catalog, constraints, party creation, and invitations.
The product state is shared: parties appear in the normal UI and invitations can reach another browser session.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and internally consistent, with a clear recommendation-to-party-to-invite workflow and a human launch decision; frames visibly show populated platform screens but not the full multiplayer completion.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows Home, Store, Library, and Friends states with consistent synthetic content.
About text states party and invitation mutations affect actual application state.
No clear launch/session result appears in the contact sheet.
impact_rationale: Groups genuinely struggle to coordinate what to play, who is available, ownership, player count, and time; the product targets that friction directly while preserving player choice.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about text specify the group-coordination problem and a concrete four-player scenario.
Social, library, presence, and catalog surfaces visibly exist.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP to turn a natural-language social gaming request into a viable multiplayer session is memorable and more ambitious than game recommendation.
creativity_evidence: Agent reasons across connected friend and game state.
Party creation and cross-session invitations extend the agent role into real coordination.
usability_note: The familiar Store/Library/Friends structure is approachable; agent coordination reduces setup burden.
red_flags: Synthetic dataset and full invitation/launch completion are described rather than clearly visible.
standouts: Strong multi-constraint social coordination use case.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and originality with a credible, concrete multiplayer coordination problem.

one_line: An aerofoil workspace for exploring geometry, loads, structure, and efficiency with agents.
what_it_does: Aeroficiency lets users create and compare wing candidates, visualize geometry and pressure behavior, and run aerodynamic/structural estimates to narrow large design spaces.
leverage_rationale: Structured design parameters and solver operations can let an agent search and compare candidates more precisely than manipulating technical controls by pixels, though the underlying workflow remains possible manually.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent-accessible design, solver, and comparison workspace.
Frames show synchronized parameter panels, 3D wing geometry, graphs, and candidate/result views.
execution_rationale: The contact sheet visibly shows a stable technical workspace with changing wing geometry and accompanying metrics/graphs, suggesting a coherent iterative analysis flow; solver validity is not independently proven.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows multiple populated design states and geometry changes.
Central visualization, controls, candidate panel, and plotted result remain coherent across frames.
No explicit agent call or numerical validation trace is legible.
impact_rationale: Early-stage aerofoil screening is a real engineering and educational need, especially when exhaustive candidate evaluation is computationally impractical.
impact_evidence: About text gives a specific wind-turbine design problem and large candidate-search motivation.
UI visibly couples geometry with analysis outputs.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native structured operations to preliminary aerodynamic and structural exploration is ambitious and unusual for a hackathon product.
creativity_evidence: Product combines 2D/3D geometry, aerodynamic loads, structural response, and efficiency.
The concept targets rapid filtering before expensive detailed analysis.
usability_note: Technical controls and dense metrics appear useful for the target audience but are not especially accessible to novices.
red_flags: Frames show application changes but not direct WebMCP invocation; solver outputs are not externally validated.
standouts: Concrete engineering problem with unusually substantial technical visualization.
advance_reason: Credible technical workspace and strong niche impact; WebMCP evidence is less direct than the top packets.

one_line: A differential-evaluation tool that finds and verifies minimal protocol changes causing result reversals.
what_it_does: MPW compares two evaluation setups, searches counterfactual protocol subsets, verifies minimality across the exposed space, and produces replay-verifiable certificates.
leverage_rationale: Semantic tools for disputes, counterfactuals, evidence, and witness verification let an agent navigate a rigorous analysis surface more reliably than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text names four domain tools: read_dispute, run_counterfactual, inspect_evidence, and verify_witness.
Frames show a generated artifact with LAB A/LAB B comparison, protocol differences, and structured evidence sections.
execution_rationale: The visible artifact is coherent and progressively populated, and the described deterministic search and full-subset verification indicate strong scope discipline; the actual certificate output is not plainly visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows initial prompt, progressive artifact generation, LAB A/LAB B comparison, and protocol-difference sections.
About text claims exact minimum-witness verification, replay certificates, and adversarial testing.
No readable tool result/certificate is shown in frames.
impact_rationale: Evaluation practitioners have a real need to explain conflicting benchmark results and distinguish protocol effects from model effects.
impact_evidence: Packet defines a specific 400-item synthetic benchmark dispute and a concrete minimum-witness question.
Evidence inspection and replay verification address scientific auditability.
creativity_rationale: Minimal counterfactual witnesses for protocol-sensitive evaluation reversals are a novel, technically ambitious interaction model with clear methodological value.
creativity_evidence: Concept isolates the smallest sufficient protocol change rather than merely comparing scores.
Non-monotonic effects and full-subset verification are explicitly handled.
usability_note: The structured comparison artifact is legible, but the research concepts are specialized.
red_flags: Synthetic benchmark and certificate completion are not directly readable in the frame sheet.
standouts: Strong separation between agent investigation and deterministic scientific verification.
advance_reason: Highly original research workflow with strong rigor claims and visible artifact construction.

one_line: A visual funk-practice sequencer for chords, rhythm placement, grooves, and drums.
what_it_does: Funk Trainer synchronizes a rhythmic grid, guitar chord voicings, key selection, groove generation, and drum practice, with agent tools for controlling those elements.
leverage_rationale: Structured musical controls let an agent translate a musical request into synchronized sequencer state with less friction than UI driving, but a skilled user could reproduce much of the outcome manually.
leverage_evidence: About text lists agent operations for key, groove, chord selection, and beat placement.
Frames show the trainer page alongside a persistent dark assistant panel with changing messages and green action-like states.
execution_rationale: Observable evidence supports a coherent visual sequencer and assistant-assisted interaction, but audio quality, timing feel, and musicality are not assessable and the exact tool result is not legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows stable trainer UI with chord/rhythm controls and an adjacent interaction panel.
About text states synchronized visual grid, guitar, and drums.
Audio-dependent behavior is treated as unknown per directive, not scored down.
impact_rationale: Learners practicing funk rhythm have a specific need for visual beat placement and coordinated accompaniment; the product addresses that learning workflow.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets guitar and drum awareness one beat at a time.
About text identifies chord placement, voicings, grooves, and play-along practice.
creativity_rationale: The visual 'where you play' emphasis and agent translation of musical requests add a meaningful new angle to a known practice-tool category.
creativity_evidence: Combines synchronized rhythm visualization, guitar fingering, and drum groove practice.
Agent can turn a reference such as Superstition into sequencer settings.
usability_note: The visual practice model appears approachable; audio usability is not assessable from silent evidence.
red_flags: Audio quality, musicality, and timing feel are not assessable; exact assistant actions are unreadable.
standouts: Good visual pedagogy for rhythm placement rather than relying only on sound.
advance_reason: Solid niche educational product with meaningful agent control; silent evidence limits confidence but not scores.

one_line: A human-controlled contract review workspace that turns agent clause analysis into actionable redlines.
what_it_does: Redline loads contracts, extracts clauses, assesses risk and enforceability context, presents decisions beside exact text, and exports a negotiation email from accepted changes.
leverage_rationale: Clause-level structured access, grounded assessments, dynamic tool registration, and write-back into exact document locations are far more reliable than asking a general agent to navigate a long PDF visually.
leverage_evidence: About text names seven tools including extract_clauses, get_clause_text, assess_clause, and export_negotiation_email.
Frames show a multi-page contract viewer, Redline workspace, WebGPT/Interact with the Page panel, and waiting-for-agent state.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent document-to-clause-decision-to-email workflow with a clear progress model, but the contact sheet stops at waiting for the agent and does not show completed redlines.
execution_evidence: Frames show contract selection, 22-page document viewing, review workspace, and agent integration state.
About text describes clarity gated on assessment and redline decisions, side-by-side current/proposed output, and reset behavior.
No completed review result is visible.
impact_rationale: People facing employment contracts and deadlines have a concrete, high-stakes comprehension problem; clause-grounded explanations and actionable negotiation language offer credible value while retaining human decisions.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about text identify employment-contract review, risk flags, grounded reasons, redlines, and negotiation email.
Frames visibly show a real multi-page employment offer in the review context.
creativity_rationale: The blur-as-progress model and exact-sentence decision cards create a memorable interaction that makes agent assessment legible without removing human authority.
creativity_evidence: Clarity is computed from clause assessment and resolved redline decisions.
Accepted changes roll into a negotiation email with current/proposed comparison.
usability_note: The document-centered review model and per-clause decisions are understandable, though legal context requires careful user judgment.
red_flags: Frame sheets show waiting for the external agent rather than a completed review; legal conclusions should not be overclaimed.
standouts: Excellent alignment between WebMCP structure and clause-level human decision-making.
advance_reason: High impact, originality, and transformative WebMCP fit; only the unshown final review limits execution confidence.

one_line: A shared 3D spatial world where agents inspect, simulate, and propose changes for human approval.
what_it_does: SynSpace exposes a versioned 3D world for object/zone inspection, measurements, constraint checks, isolated what-if scenarios, proposals, approval, attribution, and undo.
leverage_rationale: A structured world model, typed spatial operations, scenario forks, constraint evaluation, and revision-aware proposals are precisely the capabilities pixel-based browser agents cannot replicate comparably well.
leverage_evidence: About text states 30 typed tools over a shared versioned world document.
Frames visibly show a 3D viewport, world inspector, and activity/session panels transitioning into active states.
Product thesis explicitly contrasts world structure with pixels.
execution_rationale: The visual product is coherent and the described safety/consistency architecture is unusually complete, but the contact sheet does not clearly show a specific approved spatial mutation or scenario result.
execution_evidence: Frames show stable 3D scene, inspector, toolbar, and populated activity panels.
About text describes deterministic checks, isolated forks, stale-proposal detection, human approval, attribution, and undo.
Exact tool payloads and final applied change are not legible.
impact_rationale: Designers, planners, and spatial analysts can benefit from agent-assisted measurement and constraint checking in rooms, offices, and cities, with meaningful safety controls.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies room, office, and city layout use cases.
Constraint classes include collisions, spacing, egress, clearance, and walkway width.
creativity_rationale: Treating a 3D spatial world as a shared structured medium for agent reasoning and human approval is a highly original and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: One world, two minds framing is implemented through shared state rather than a chat wrapper.
What-if forks and before/after metrics deepen the concept.
usability_note: The inspector and visual world aid understanding, but spatial tooling is inherently more complex than ordinary forms.
red_flags: Contact sheet includes an editing watermark; direct completed proposal approval is not visible.
standouts: Most compelling demonstration of WebMCP changing the representational substrate from pixels to structured world state.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and originality with a coherent, safety-conscious spatial workflow.
